name: Bushrangers Bay
address: Cape Schanck Rd, Cape Schanck VIC 3939
signature: A remote, wild bay accessible only on foot — basalt rock platforms, blow holes, and the most dramatic coastal scenery on the Peninsula
editorNote:
Bushrangers Bay is reached via a 45-minute walk from the Cape Schanck car park — steep in parts, uneven, and worth every minute. The bay itself is a wild, usually deserted crescent of black basalt sand flanked by volcanic rock platforms and backed by coastal heathland. The blow holes activate on a decent swell and the rock platforms are extraordinary at low tide.

This is not a swimming beach — the shore break and rips are serious and the beach is completely unpatrolled. It is a place to walk to, stand on, and look at. The walk back via the clifftop gives a second perspective on the cape that is different again.

Bring water, wear shoes with grip, and time it for low tide if you want the rock platforms. The walk from Cape Schanck lighthouse makes a logical combined visit.
whyWeGo: The most remote and dramatic beach on the Peninsula — worth the walk every single time.
ifOnlyOneThing: Time it to arrive at low tide and walk the rock platforms south of the bay. The blow holes are best on a 3ft+ swell.
